aggregate_initial_judgment: Read before opening seat totals. Claim: a retrained waypoint predictor (DINOv2, masked cross-attention RGB-D fusion, depth-derived occupancy loss) plus a zero-shot GPT-4o navigator that sees candidate-waypoint images, history with RAM tags, multi-scale turns, a carried plan and a one-step 'move back' option, reaching zero-shot SOTA on the Open-Nav 100-episode R2R-CE subset (SR 29, SPL 22.46) and 9/25 on a Turtlebot 4. Evidence: Table I single run vs copied zero-shot rows with other models; Table V 2x2 (predictor x backtrack) whose check-mark columns are lost in extraction but whose rows are pinned by the text (#1 baseline, #3 enhanced predictor only, #2/#4 with backtrack, #4 full) except one narrative NE value; Tables III/IV offline waypoint metrics that disagree with each other for the same full model (1.41 vs 1.48); 25 physical instructions, one trial each. The 'first exploration of MLLMs in VLN-CE' claim is contradicted by the paper's own MapGPT-CE-GPT4o row. Expected: transfer (counted sim-to-real), scoped support, E around 2, statistics 1.

gap.author_gap: Waypoint predictors ignore environmental constraints and under-use RGB; LLM navigators for VLN-CE rely on text conversions of images and lack history-aware reasoning and backtracking.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and partly quantified (about 20% of baseline waypoints fall in obstructed areas, %Open ~80). Lineage clear (Hong et al. predictor, Open-Nav, MapGPT, DiscussNav). Two residue boundaries are weak: the large OSR-SR gap (51 vs 29), i.e. stopping, is not analysed, and the 'first MLLM in VLN-CE' framing is contradicted by the paper's own MapGPT-CE-GPT4o row (agg:G05/G06).
